{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Filter to completed orders only
completed_df = df[df['status'] == 'completed']

# Verify premises

# Premise 1: email campaign targeted at high-value customers → confirmed by segment imbalance
# Premise 2: six QA orders with revenue = 999999.99 → check
qa_mask = df['revenue'] == '999999.99'
num_qa = len(df[qa_mask])
print(f"Number of QA orders: {num_qa}")

# Premise 3: refunded orders are included → yes, 85
refunded_count = len(df[df['status'] == 'refunded'])
print(f"Number of refunded orders: {refunded_count}")

# Premise 4: channel not randomly assigned → known from doc and confirmed by segment imbalance
# Premise 5: email aimed at loyal customers who buy more → confirmed by higher loyal segment in email

# Now, compute within-segment conversion rates
channel_segment_conv = completed_df.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'])['converted'].mean().reset_index()
pivot = channel_segment_conv.pivot(index='customer_segment', columns='channel', values='converted')

# Compute differences
pivot['diff'] = pivot['email'] - pivot['paid_search']

# Get segment proportions
segment_prop = completed_df['customer_segment'].value_counts(normalize=True)

# Compute weighted average difference
weighted_diff = (pivot['diff'] * segment_prop).sum()
value = weighted_diff * 100

# Print all required numbers as they appear in the output
print("\nWithin-segment conversion rates (email):")
print(pivot['email'])

print("\nWithin-segment conversion rates (paid_search):")
print(pivot['paid_search'])

print("\nWithin-segment differences (email - paid_search):")
print(pivot['diff'])

print("\nSegment proportions in completed orders:")
print(segment_prop)

print(f"\nWeighted difference: {weighted_diff:.6f} (i.e. {value:.3f} percentage points)")"}
